answer: Equivocation slashing stops one identity from selling two clashing proofs per epoch. Both proofs sit under a lantern, where observers compare signatures. A Sybil operator who tries to forge a second proof loses 30% of its 100-credit stake and freezes an epoch. The k-th fake costs as much as the first, its own 100-credit stake, and cannot reuse another proof, because reuse is the equivocation the lantern catches; proof rental fails. For 1,000 fakes the operator risks 100,000 credits, while an honest agent files one proof, passes as a zephyr, and keeps its stake.
